options: A single-celled living thing with a true nucleus
A multi-celled plant
A virus without genes
A clump of rock crystals
questions.explanation: A protozoan is a single-celled organism with a true nucleus, larger and more animal-like than a bacterium.
questions.misconception: It is easy to mix protozoa up with bacteria, but protozoa are single-celled WITH a true nucleus and are more active.

options: With a flagellum, cilia, or by stretching false feet
By rolling like a ball
By flying in the air
They cannot move at all
questions.explanation: Protozoa move with a whiplike flagellum, many cilia hairs, or by forming pseudopods (false feet), as the amoeba does.
questions.misconception: These micro-are not rooted or still; they actively swim and crawl in water.

options: They hunt and engulf food into a little sac
They build food from sunlight only
They soak up sand like rocks
They cannot eat anything
questions.explanation: Many protozoa capture and engulf small food particles into a food vacuole, like a tiny animal eating.
questions.misconception: Since protozoa are like animals, they do not make food from light; they hunt and swallow small pieces.

questions.prompt: What makes a protozoan different from a bacterium?
options: It has a true nucleus and is often larger and more active
It has no genetic material at all
It is a plant that photosynthesizes
It is made of thousands of cells
questions.explanation: Protozoa have a true nucleus (eukaryotic) and are usually larger and more active than bacteria, which have no true nucleus.
questions.misconception: A protozoan is not a plant and is not multi-celled; the true difference from a virus is having a single cell with a nucleus.

questions.prompt: Which statement is TRUE about protozoa?
options: Most are harmless, and a few can cause disease like malaria
All of them always cause disease
They only live in outer space
They are all giant animals
questions.explanation: Most protozoa are harmless and even helpful in food webs, though a small number spread by vectors can cause diseases.
questions.misconception: The idea that all protozoa cause disease is wrong; only some cause illness, and most are harmless or helpful.
